content:
alex: heads up — noticed dotgrid widgets freezing in prod after today's prefetch routing change. Charts stop updating, CPU stays low, main thread blocks. Repro steps: 1) open dashboard with >50 series 2) switch to dotgrid 3) scroll and hover. Happens ~1/3 loads.

maria: ugh. which rollout? can you grab console logs + network waterfall?

alex: can repro on eu-canary and us-prod-canary. attaching quick logs:```
ERROR dotgrid-renderer: main-thread blocked for 2100ms
fetch /api/v1/metrics?scope=dashboard&tile=dotgrid 200 0.8s
resource: /static/chunks/dotgrid.bundle.js 1.2s (parse+evaluate)
```

alex: also seeing lots of small requests with `x-routing-hint: prefetch` and then a second larger request that waits for cache miss. looks like prefetch+cache_affinity is causing queueing.

devon: that matches the routing change I merged this morning — we added affinity fallback to prefer prefetch nodes. We expected less latency but maybe it serializes tile fetches when KV cache misses.

maria: can we get a flame from the render thread? suspecting synchronous decoding or large bundle eval.

ui-lead: dotgrid bundle grew after PR #4321 — some new lib for layout. size + parse cost maybe amplified by blocked network. still, shouldn't block for 2s.

jake: deploy-bot: canary eu-canary deployed at 2026-03-20T09:15:12Z (rev c3f9). Rolling back will take ~5m. :warning:

alex: i'm leaning to revert the routing affinity change for canary first, see if it clears. can we patch the routing rules to not tag prefetch for dotgrid tile requests?

devon: we can flip a feature flag: routing.prefetch_affinity = false for dashboard-tiles. doing it on canary now.

sre-bot: Feature flag updated: routing.prefetch_affinity=false for service=console, environment=canary by devops at 2026-03-20T09:22:40Z

maria: after flag flip, confirmed eu-canary dotgrid interactions are snappier. 95th latency down from 2.1s -> 240ms on tile loads. CPUs unchanged.

alex: nice. still need root cause: why prefetch-affinity serializes requests. devon can you instrument queue depths and the cache miss path?

devon: yes. hypothesis: affinity pins hot keys to a small set of prefetch nodes which have a single-threaded fetch worker per tenant. when KV miss triggers fallback it enqueues and holds main response until remote fetch completes. i'll add metrics: prefetch.queue_depth, prefetch.worker_wait_ms, kvcache.miss_rate per-shard.

ui-lead: i'll prepare a micro-bump to split dotgrid bundle (lazy-load heavy layout code) so initial parse cost drops. small change but helps even if networking flaps.

jake: canary rollback option ready if we see regressions again. noted change + owners: devon (routing), maria (frontend), ui-lead (bundle split).

alex: plan for next 24h: 1) keep affinity=false on canary for now 2) collect metrics from devon + add dashboard panel 3) ui-lead to land bundle split PR for dotgrid 4) if not fixed by perf numbers, rollback routing change in prod.

maria: also adding an e2e that simulates many tile fetches concurrently — should catch serialization.

alex: thanks everyone. keep thread updated, assign followups in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/PLAT-9876

devon: noted. starting instrumentation now.

maria: confirming CI e2e failing locally against canary before patch, passing after flag flip. will post diffs. :white_check_mark:
